# Adversarial Source/PIT Review — Q202–Q204 + Q205 (Worker Material)

Status: REVIEW_COMPLETE_ON_EMBEDDED_ARTIFACTS. This is worker material only, not scientific evidence. No returns/holdouts inspected, no assets/parameters/thresholds/horizons selected, no gates altered, no performance/promotion/live authorization implied. All source-feasibility readiness below is treated as PROVISIONAL.

## Scope note on what was actually inspectable
- Q202–Q204: only a pointer to `q202_q204_information_timing_feasibility_latest.json` is visible; the receipt body was not supplied. Compiler maps Q202/Q203/Q204 → `IMMUTABLE_HISTORICAL_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED_BEFORE_PIT`.
- Q205 (NLRB labor-representation certification): discovery-only, and it is absent from both `source_readiness_snapshot_guard.RECEIPTS` and `orthogonal_pit_next_gate.RECEIPTS/NEXT_GATES`. It has no deterministic gate wired at all.
- The Grok Q194–Q201 standard (current reachability/hashes ≠ durable PIT proof) is accepted and extended.

## Findings (adversarial)

1. The durability guard is too permissive to enforce the universal rule. `has_durable_binding()` returns True on mere truthy presence of any `DURABLE_KEYS` entry (e.g. `snapshot_sha256`, `archive_fingerprint`). It does not check that the value is a dated vintage, that the hash resolves to an immutable artifact, or that it is bound to the specific candidate. A receipt carrying a hash of a *current* page would classify as `DURABLE_HISTORICAL_BOUND` — the exact failure the rule forbids. I disagree with treating this guard output as sufficient readiness evidence.

2. "latest" receipts are mutable by construction. `..._feasibility_latest.json` naming implies overwrite-on-rerun. A readiness claim resting on a "latest" file has no vintage identity and cannot be reproduced as-of a date.

3. Q205 is ungated and unbacked. Any statement that Q205 is "source/PIT ready" is an unsupported worker assertion; there is no receipt, no compiler entry, no next-gate. Discovery-only status is being implicitly treated as more than it is.

4. Spec/compiler lineage mismatch. The compiler loads `orthogonal_candidate_specs_2026-10-05.json`; the supplied contract file is `..._2026-10-04.json`. Which vintage is authoritative is unresolved — a mapping/lineage drift risk.

5. Real cross-publication date conflict already exists in-repo. CURRENT_STATUS documents SEC 13F `SUBMISSION.FILING_DATE` differing from EDGAR header date by one day (2015-02-18 vs 02-17; 2020-08-10 vs 08-07). This is a concrete instance of the date-only/revision-lineage hazard and shows date fields are not safe to arithmetic-over.

6. Temporal inconsistency in the evidence chain. Task/review artifacts are dated 2026-10-04; CURRENT_STATUS is generated 2026-11-26 and is declared canonical. The operational snapshot postdates the artifacts under review; do not silently reconcile.

7. Q202–Q204 orthogonality is unproven. All three sit in one "information-timing" family and plausibly share a single upstream publication clock (SEC/EDGAR). Shared upstream ⇒ convergence, not orthogonality, among the three.

## Counterarguments / preserved disagreement
- Counter to my point 1: the guard is a fail-closed *audit*, not the gate itself, and the compiler still emits `IMMUTABLE_HISTORICAL_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED_BEFORE_PIT`. Rebuttal: an audit that can be satisfied by a current-page hash still produces a misleading `DURABLE_HISTORICAL_BOUND` label that downstream humans may trust. Disagreement preserved.
- Counter to point 7: Q205 (NLRB) is a genuinely distinct source class and improves frontier orthogonality. Agreed — but establishment→issuer mapping may overlap Q195 facility exposure, so orthogonality is candidate-pair-specific, not family-level.
- I do not assert Q202–Q204 or Q205 are infeasible; I assert readiness is unproven on durable
